expectations.text: The response asks for the exact MariaDB version and gives a command to get it (e.g. SELECT VERSION())
expectations.evidence: 'Check what prod is running ... SELECT VERSION();'

expectations.text: The response recommends an index led by status followed by due_date ASC and amount DESC, matching the mixed-direction ORDER BY
expectations.evidence: Case A: '(status, due_date ASC, amount DESC, customer_id)'

expectations.text: The response states that descending index parts are only honored from MariaDB 10.8 (older versions parse but ignore DESC, so the sort cannot be served by the index)
expectations.evidence: 'Real descending indexes only arrived in MariaDB 10.8. Before 10.8, MariaDB accepts DESC in an index definition but ignores it'

expectations.text: The response gives a concrete fallback for MariaDB < 10.8 (e.g. index (status, due_date) and sorting only the ties, or a persistent/virtual generated column such as negated amount)
expectations.evidence: Case B Option 1 'neg_amount ... AS (-amount) VIRTUAL' index; Option 2 (status, due_date, amount); Option 3 change ordering

expectations.text: The response does not recommend MySQL-8-only syntax as if it works in MariaDB (e.g. functional index key parts like INDEX ((expr)), or INVISIBLE instead of MariaDB's IGNORED)
expectations.evidence: No MySQL-8-only syntax; uses virtual generated column, plain DROP INDEX

expectations.text: The response gives a MariaDB plan command for verification (ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON SELECT ... or EXPLAIN) and says what to look for (no filesort, rows vs r_rows)
expectations.evidence: EXPLAIN + 'ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON SELECT ..., which reports the rows actually read'; 'Extra does not show Using filesort'

expectations.text: The response asks for data volume / selectivity of status = 'overdue' or its distribution
expectations.evidence: 'Roughly how many rows have status = overdue (SELECT COUNT(*) ...)'

expectations.text: The response asks about traffic or write rate on invoices
expectations.evidence: Never asks about page traffic or write/update rate on invoices; only mentions write overhead of keeping idx_status
